title: Terraform module release process: SemVer, tags, changelog, and maintainer checklist
creator: Irene Choi
content:
## Context
We’re about to start design partner pilots for the Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha). Teams in the field need a predictable way to pin versions, and Infra needs a repeatable process for cutting releases without hand-editing changelogs.

This ticket implements and documents the release process for `redwood-terraform` modules:
- Semantic versioning (SemVer) rules for alpha
- Tagging conventions and GitHub Releases
- Changelog generation discipline
- A maintainer review checklist (what must be true before we cut a release)

## Goals
1) Release process is boring and repeatable: maintainers can cut a release with a single workflow.
2) Customers/design partners can pin module versions (via git tag) and understand what changed.
3) Clear compatibility commitments for alpha (Terraform/AWS provider versions).
4) Changelog is actionable (what changed, impact, migration notes when needed).

## Non-goals
- Publishing to the public Terraform Registry (alpha scope is GitHub releases + tags; internal docs can describe registry as future work).
- Building a full policy engine for what constitutes a breaking change (we’ll document rules + require human review).

## Proposed release policy (alpha)
### Tag format
- Repo-level tags: `vX.Y.Z` (e.g., `v0.3.1`)
- GitHub Release name mirrors tag

Rationale: customers pin to a single repo revision for a known-good module suite; we avoid per-module version drift during alpha.

### SemVer interpretation
- **MAJOR (X)**: Breaking changes to any module interface or behavior that could force resource replacement or require configuration changes. Examples:
  - Renaming/removing inputs/outputs
  - Changing default subnet or NAT strategy
  - Changing endpoint private DNS defaults
  - Changing logging destinations/retention defaults in a way that affects audit posture
- **MINOR (Y)**: Backward-compatible features. Examples:
  - New optional inputs (default off)
  - Additional supported endpoints with conservative defaults
  - New examples / documentation
- **PATCH (Z)**: Backward-compatible fixes. Examples:
  - Bugfixes in routing tables, AZ mapping
  - Docs corrections
  - CI/test harness fixes

### “Breaking change” rule of thumb (what maintainers should look for)
If an existing design partner `tfvars` file that worked with the previous version would:
- fail `terraform plan`, OR
- show planned replacement of core networking resources (VPC/Subnets/Route Tables/NAT/VPC Endpoints), OR
- change security posture by default (new public egress path, reduced logging)
…then treat it as **MAJOR** and include explicit migration notes.

## Compatibility commitments
- Terraform: `>= 1.6.x` (pinned in CI; documented in README)
- AWS provider: pinned to a compatible minor series (document exact constraint used in repo; update only in MINOR or MAJOR)
- Module support target: AWS commercial regions; GovCloud explicitly “best-effort” until we validate endpoints + logging parity

## Implementation (what changed)
1) Added a release workflow (GitHub Actions):
   - On manual dispatch with a version bump (major/minor/patch), run:
     - `terraform fmt -check`
     - `terraform validate` (all example stacks)
     - `tflint` (repo config)
     - `checkov` (baseline policies for network exposure + logging)
     - integration test job (ephemeral VPC) gates release if enabled; otherwise requires a maintainer attestation for same-day hotfixes
   - Generate changelog entries from merged PR titles + labels; require “Release note” section in PR template for anything user-facing
   - Create tag `vX.Y.Z` and GitHub Release; attach a source archive

2) Changelog rules:
   - `CHANGELOG.md` at repo root; append-only
   - Sections: Added / Changed / Fixed / Security / Breaking Changes
   - Every MAJOR release must include a “Migration” subsection with concrete steps

3) Documentation:
   - Added `docs/releasing.md` with:
     - How to decide bump type
     - How to run release workflow
     - What to validate locally when CI is flaky
     - How to communicate a release to design partners (pinning guidance)

4) Maintainer checklist (release gate)
### Pre-flight
- [ ] All required CI checks are green on `main`
- [ ] Integration test (ephemeral VPC) is green within last 24h OR documented exception (hotfix)
- [ ] No open P0/P1 issues tagged `release-blocker`
- [ ] Provider constraints unchanged OR bump type chosen accordingly

### Terraform interface & state risk review
- [ ] Reviewed diffs for any changes to: VPC/Subnet CIDRs, NAT strategy, Route Tables, Endpoint private DNS, Flow Logs destinations
- [ ] Confirmed no unintended resource replacement in the example `terraform plan` output
- [ ] If any replacement is expected, release is MAJOR and migration notes are included

### Security posture
- [ ] Defaults still: private subnets for workloads, no inbound public access by default, logging enabled by default (Flow Logs)
- [ ] Any new permissions in IAM scaffold reviewed (diff checked)

### Docs + examples
- [ ] README updated if inputs/outputs changed
- [ ] Example `tfvars` and quickstart still apply
- [ ] Release notes include known limitations + support escalation path

### Cut release
- [ ] Run workflow with bump type and confirm generated tag `vX.Y.Z`
- [ ] Post release link to `#eng-infra` and `#support` with 3 bullets: what changed, risk, who to contact

## Acceptance criteria
- Release can be cut without editing files by hand other than changelog fragments / PR release notes
- Tags and releases follow a consistent naming convention
- Changelog includes meaningful entries for the last 5 merged PRs (validated by maintainers)
- Maintainer checklist exists and is referenced in repo docs
- Design partner guidance: pinned version and upgrade coordination documented (link to alpha upgrade notes)

## Links
- Confluence standard: `terraform-module-versioning-and-release-process` (align wording/commitments)
- Related work: release automation PR (tracked separately)
- Pilot coordination: alpha upgrade notes for design partners

## Rollout plan
- Dogfood: cut `v0.1.0` from current `main` after checklist is satisfied
- For alpha pilots: recommend pinning exact `v0.x.y` tag, and only upgrading on Redwood-led weekly check-in

## Open questions / follow-ups
- Whether to require signed tags (GPG) for GA
- Whether to publish to Terraform Registry as part of GA (needs packaging decision: per-module vs suite)
- Whether integration tests run per-PR or nightly only (cost/time vs confidence trade-off)
comments: 2025-06-24 (Irene Choi): We’ve hit version confusion twice already in sandbox + field demos. Please make it dead-simple for SEs to say “use v0.2.0” and know what’s inside.

2025-06-27 (Connor O'Brien): Drafted SemVer rules. Biggest ambiguity is what we call “breaking” for default changes (e.g., endpoint private DNS). Proposed rule: if it changes plan for existing tfvars, it’s breaking.

2025-07-01 (Sahana Iyer): CI can gate tagging on fmt/validate/tflint/checkov. Integration tests should be optional for hotfixes but must have an explicit attestation step; otherwise we’ll block patch releases during AWS service hiccups.

2025-07-03 (Naomi Feldman): Please ensure changelog has a dedicated “Security” section. Also call out any logging destination/retention changes as security-relevant even if technically backward compatible.

2025-07-08 (Victor Alvarez): +1 on treating NAT/subnet changes as MAJOR. Even a “default only” change can force replacement depending on how the module is wired; checklist should explicitly require reviewing plan output from examples.
2025-07-15 (Devon Price): Suggest using PR labels to map to changelog sections (enhancement/fix/security/breaking). This keeps generated notes readable and reduces maintainer burden.

2025-07-22 (Connor O'Brien): Merged release docs + checklist. Ran a dry-run release in a fork; tagging + GitHub Release creation works. Next: cut v0.1.0 once ENG-4860 integration tests are green in main CI.
